subject: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs Nimbusify (Orchid Labs)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamie Ford <jamie.ford@orchidlabs.com>; Priya Shah <priya.shah@orchidlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs Nimbusify (Orchid Labs)

Hi Jamie / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the bake-off:

Top pain points you highlighted:
- Latency spikes during batch inference for the docs summarization pipeline (95th percentile > 800ms)
- Cost pressure for peak-hour throughput — current spend projection +40% if we scale without optimizations
- Need for data isolation and audit logs for HIPAA readiness (SOC2 in progress but want stricter access controls)

Goals you shared:
- Match current throughput with <=250ms P95 for interactive summarization (per 1k concurrent users)
- Reduce per-token inference cost by 30% vs current setup during steady-state
- Proof of concept completed within 3 weeks for decision by May 6

Summary of vendor comparison notes from today:
- Redwood: strong batching + KV prefix cache, route-by-policy for burst capacity, private deployment option with KMS support
- Nimbusify: claims lower nominal latency on single-request microbenchmarks but less transparent cost controls and fewer audit log features

Open technical questions we will run in the POC/test harness (see attached test plan):
1) End-to-end P95 latency with concurrent sessions (1k concurrent) using your sample corpus
2) Token cost under 5-minute steady-state with realistic request distribution
3) Behavior under model fallbacks (e.g., quantized variants) including quality checks

Next steps (proposed):
- We will provision a short-lived dedicated test pool and run the three tests above using your corpus. ETA: 4 business days once we get access details.
- Please share S3 access to the sample corpus + a minimal subset of production traffic for realistic load testing.
- Marissa / Rishi: can you confirm resource availability for a 4-day bake-off starting 2027-04-19?

Attachments: redwood_bakeoff_summary.pdf (quick slides), orchid_mvp-test-plan.md (test steps)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to align on details.

Best,
Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0182

Thanks Jamie / team —

Quick technical notes from Rishi (solutions engineering):
- 24h audit log export: yes, we can provide an export of IAM and runtime events in JSONL (fields: timestamp, user, action, resource, status). We'll include an example schema in the drive link.
- For the latency tests, we'll run both cold-start and warm-KV-cache scenarios. Warm-cache targets are realistic for your production patterns.
- We'll instrument token-level cost reporting and provide a cost breakdown by model variant and batch size.

Requesting two things from Orchid to start infra prep:
1) S3 read-only credentials for s3://orchid-bakeoff/sample-corpus (per Jamie)
2) A small representative traffic profile (CSV) with fields: timestamp, request_size_tokens, session_id

Plan: provision dedicated test pool on 4/18, run tests 4/19-4/22, share results and a short 30-min review call on 4/23.

Marissa: can you prepare the performance summary slide (P95 boxes/throughput/cost) and drop the preliminary PDF in the drive link by 4/18 EOD?

-Rishi

Hi all —

I uploaded a first-pass performance summary PDF to the shared drive (link above) and included preliminary guidance on quantization profiles and batching settings that should hit your cost/latency targets. High-level notes:
- Expected P95 (warm-cache, 1k concurrent): ~220-280ms depending on model quantization; will measure precisely during run.
- Cost delta: with batching + prefix cache we estimate ~28-35% cost reduction vs your baseline at steady-state.
- Fallback quality: we'll run automated quality checks using your eval set; if quantization introduces >2% accuracy delta on key metrics, we'll flag for manual review.

Next immediate asks from Orchid: please confirm.
1) S3 credentials delivery channel (Priya / Jamie)
2) Approval to spin up the short-lived dedicated pool (4/18 start) — this will incur a modest daily reserved cost for the test window.

If approved, we will share the final runbook and a DocuSign link for a short POC addendum (covers test pool scope & data handling) — aiming to have that signed by 4/18 morning.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick sync if you want to walk the runbook.

Best,
